cases.sentence: Но ___ этот был целый мир для Левина.
cases.translation: But this house was a whole world for Levin.
cases.explain: Дом is the grammatical subject of был (was), so it stands in the nominative case.

cases.sentence: Через два года будут у меня в ___ две голландки.
cases.translation: In two years I will have two Dutch cows in my herd.
cases.explain: The preposition в (in) governs the prepositional case, giving стаде.

cases.sentence: На те деньги, что ему подарил Левин, чтобы лошадь купить, пьет без просопу и ___ избил до смерти.
cases.translation: With the money Levin gave him to buy a horse, he drinks nonstop and beat his wife nearly to death.
cases.explain: Жену is the direct object of the transitive verb избил (beat), so it is accusative.

cases.sentence: Будущая жена его должна была быть повторением того идеала ___, каким была для него мать.
cases.translation: His future wife had to be a repetition of the ideal of woman that his mother had been for him.
cases.explain: Женщины depends on идеала (ideal of), a noun-modifying genitive.

cases.sentence: Он подошел к ___, где у него стояли две пудовые гири.
cases.translation: He went over to the corner where he kept two heavy weights.
cases.explain: The preposition к (toward) governs the dative case, giving углу.

cases.sentence: Понятие о ней было для него священным ___.
cases.translation: The idea of her was for him a sacred memory.
cases.explain: Воспоминанием is the predicate noun after было ... для него (was a memory), governed instrumentally by быть.

cases.sentence: Когда он вошел в маленькую ___, где всегда пил чай, и уселся в своем кресле.
cases.translation: When he entered the small drawing room, where he always drank tea, and settled into his armchair.
cases.explain: The preposition в (into) with motion governs the accusative case, giving гостиную.

cases.sentence: Он вспоминал свои осуждения ___ за его самодовольство.
cases.translation: He recalled his criticisms of Tyndall for his self-satisfaction.
cases.explain: Осуждение governs the dative case for the person criticized, giving Тиндалю.

reading.ru: Дом был большой, старинный, и Левин, хотя жил один, но топил и занимал весь дом.
reading.question: What kind of house did Levin live in?
options: A large, old house that he heated and occupied entirely, though living alone
A house he shared with several tenants
reading.correct: A large, old house that he heated and occupied entirely, though living alone
reading.explain: The text says Дом был большой, старинный, и Левин ... топил и занимал весь дом.

reading.ru: Но дом этот был целый мир для Левина.
reading.question: What did the house mean to Levin?
options: It was an entire world to him
It was just a burden to maintain
It meant nothing special to him
reading.correct: It was an entire world to him
reading.explain: The text says дом этот был целый мир для Левина.

reading.ru: Это был мир, в котором жили и умерли его отец и мать.
reading.question: Why was the house so significant to Levin?
options: His father and mother had lived and died there
It was built by his own hands
He had been born abroad and only recently bought it
It once belonged to Sergei Ivanovich
reading.correct: His father and mother had lived and died there
reading.explain: The text says it was the world в котором жили и умерли его отец и мать.

reading.question: How well did Levin remember his mother?
options: He remembered her vividly and in detail
He had no memory of her existence
reading.explain: The text says Левин едва помнил свою мать — Levin barely remembered his mother.

reading.ru: Любовь к женщине он не только не мог себе представить без брака, но он прежде представлял себе семью, а потом уже ту женщину, которая даст ему семью.
reading.question: How did Levin conceive of love and marriage?
options: He imagined the family first, and only then the woman who would give it to him
He believed love had nothing to do with marriage
He wanted a wife before even considering a family
He rejected the idea of marriage altogether
reading.correct: He imagined the family first, and only then the woman who would give it to him
reading.explain: The text says he прежде представлял себе семью, а потом уже ту женщину, которая даст ему семью.

reading.ru: Это было главным делом жизни, от которого зависело все ее счастье.
reading.question: How important was marriage to Levin, compared to most of his acquaintances?
options: For him it was the main business of life, on which all happiness depended
It was one trivial matter among many, as for his acquaintances
He considered it unimportant compared to his career
He thought only wealth determined happiness
reading.correct: For him it was the main business of life, on which all happiness depended
reading.explain: The text says marriage was for him главным делом жизни, от которого зависело все ее счастье, unlike his acquaintances.

reading.ru: Он слушал разговор Агафьи Михайловны о том, как Прохор Бога забыл, и на те деньги, что ему подарил Левин, чтобы лошадь купить, пьет без просопу и жену избил до смерти.
reading.question: What did Agafya Mikhailovna tell Levin about Prokhor?
options: That Prokhor drank up the money meant for a horse and nearly beat his wife to death
That Prokhor had bought a fine new horse
That Prokhor had left the village for good
That Prokhor had repaid all his debts
reading.correct: That Prokhor drank up the money meant for a horse and nearly beat his wife to death
reading.explain: The text says Prokhor pьет без просопу и жену избил до смерти with the money Levin gave him for a horse.

reading.ru: Через два года будут у меня в стаде две голландки, сама Пава еще может быть жива, двенадцать молодых беркутовых дочерей, да подсыпать к ним наказовый конец этих трех.
reading.question: What joyful thought about his herd occurred to Levin?
options: In two years he would have a much larger, improved herd including Pava's offspring
That his entire herd would be sold off
That he should abandon cattle breeding
reading.correct: In two years he would have a much larger, improved herd including Pava's offspring
reading.explain: Levin imagines that through two years будут у меня в стаде две голландки ... двенадцать молодых беркутовых дочерей.

reading.ru: Старая ласка, еще не совсем переварившая радость его приезда, и бегавшая, чтобы полаять на дворе, вернулась, махая хвостом и внося с собой запах воздуха, подошла к нему, подсунула голову под его руку, жалобно подвизгивая и требуя, чтобы он полоскал.
reading.question: How did the old dog Laska behave when she returned?
options: She wagged her tail, nuzzled her head under his hand, and whimpered for attention
She growled and refused to come near him
She had run away and did not return
She fell asleep immediately by the door
reading.correct: She wagged her tail, nuzzled her head under his hand, and whimpered for attention
reading.explain: The text says Laska вернулась, махая хвостом ... подсунула голову под его руку, жалобно подвизгивая.
